why: Avro Vulcan B.2 flight-deck canopy: mostly metal, a smooth fairing blended into the dorsal hump, with a wrapping row of small thick heavily framed panes. The layout is read off the original model's own frame lumps (checks/orig): its windscreen bars (element 125 at x 0.19 .. 0.24 from y 5.43 at z 12.12 to 5.09 at 12.66; elements 124 / 122 at x 0.58 .. 0.73) split the front into FIVE openings (the description of the real B.2 gives a five-panel windscreen): the centre one between the inner posts, the one in front of each pilot, and a corner one each side wrapping round the rounded plan; plus the slit the model leaves between its rail and its shoulder lumps as a small side opening each side. Each pane is one flat parallelogram of a post line and a horizontal-ish direction (planar by construction); the model has no roof windows and neither does this. Pane sizes and the real aircraft's exact layout are not documented with dimensions, so they are the model's own line and UNVERIFIED against the real jet (see canopy_vulcan_b2.py). The rear crew compartment has no windows and no glass.
